metadata.source: RBI Master Directions, Ministry of Law & Justice, IBBI, DICGC

acts.commenced: March 16, 1949 (Originally Banking Companies Act, 1949; renamed in 1966)
acts.applicability: Applies to all banking companies in India, including Cooperative Banks (via Banking Regulation (Amendment) Act 2020)

key_sections.detail: Accepting, for the purpose of lending or investment, of deposits of money from the public, repayable on demand or otherwise, and withdrawable by cheque, draft, order or otherwise.
RBI approval required for appointment, re-appointment, or termination of Wholetime Directors/CEOs.
Empowers RBI to issue policy directives on loans, margins, interest rates, and loan purposes.
Mandates that no company can carry on banking business in India without a licence issued by RBI.
Prescribes maintenance of liquid assets (Cash, Gold, G-Secs) up to 40% of NDTL.

key_sections.topic: Power of RBI to Give Directions
key_sections.detail: Sweeping power to issue binding directions in public interest, banking policy, or depositor protection.
RBI power to prepare scheme of reconstruction or amalgamation of stressed banks.

acts.full_form: Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002
acts.commenced: June 21, 2002 (enacted on recommendations of Narasimham Committee II & Andhyarujina Committee)
acts.objective: Empowers secured lenders (banks/FIs) to seize, manage, and auction mortgaged residential or commercial properties to recover NPAs WITHOUT the intervention of any court or tribunal.

enforcement_process.duration: Bank serves 60 days written notice to borrower demanding full repayment.
Borrower may raise objection within 60 days; bank must reply within 15 days.
If loan remains unpaid after 60 days, bank takes physical possession of mortgaged asset.
Aggrieved borrower can appeal before Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT) within 45 days of possession.

exemptions: Agricultural land CANNOT be seized under SARFAESI Act (Section 31(i)).
Loans where remaining principal debt is LESS than ₹1 Lakh.
Cases where remaining unpaid debt balance is LESS than 20% of the original principal.

cersai.full_form: Central Electronic Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India
cersai.purpose: Government company registered under Section 8 of Companies Act 2013 to maintain a central online registry of security interests created over properties to prevent fraudulent multiple mortgages on the same property.

acts.regulator: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) - established October 1, 2016 in New Delhi

adjudicating_authorities.nclt: National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) - handles insolvency of Corporate Debtors & LLPs
adjudicating_authorities.nclat: National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) - hears appeals against NCLT orders
adjudicating_authorities.drt: Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT) - adjudicates insolvency and bankruptcy of Individuals and Partnership firms

cirp_timeline.initial_period: 180 days from the date of admission of insolvency application
cirp_timeline.one_time_extension: Up to 90 days (if approved by Committee of Creditors with 66% vote)
cirp_timeline.mandatory_outer_limit: 330 days maximum (including time taken in legal proceedings/litigation)

committee_of_creditors_coc.composition: All Financial Creditors of the corporate debtor
committee_of_creditors_coc.decision_threshold: Minimum 66% voting share required for approving Resolution Plan or replacement of Resolution Professional (RP)

acts.act_name: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) Act, 1961
acts.current_insurance_limit: ₹5,00,000 (₹5 Lakh) per depositor per insured bank (increased from ₹1 Lakh on Feb 4, 2020)
acts.coverage_details: Covers Principal + Accrued Interest across all deposit accounts (Savings, Current, Fixed, Recurring) in the same capacity and same right across all branches of that bank.
acts.premium: Paid entirely by the insured bank (presently 12 paise per ₹100 of assessable deposits per annum). Depositors pay ZERO premium.
acts.amendment_2021: DICGC (Amendment) Act 2021 mandates payment of insured deposit up to ₹5 Lakh to depositors within 90 days if a bank is placed under RBI all-inclusive directions/moratorium.
exemptions_from_insurance: Deposits of Central and State Governments
Inter-bank deposits (deposits of one bank in another bank)
Any amount due on account of any deposit received outside India

acts.act_name: Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002 & KYC Rules
acts.statutory_authority: Financial Intelligence Unit - India (FIU-IND), established in 2004 under Ministry of Finance

mandatory_reports.threshold: All cash transactions of the value of more than ₹10 Lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency (or series of integrally connected cash transactions exceeding ₹10 Lakh in a month).
mandatory_reports.submission_deadline: To FIU-IND by the 15th day of the succeeding month.

mandatory_reports.threshold: Any transaction that gives rise to reasonable ground of suspicion regarding proceeds of crime or terror financing, irrespective of transaction amount.
mandatory_reports.submission_deadline: To FIU-IND within 7 working days of arriving at a conclusion of suspicion.

mandatory_reports.threshold: All cash transactions where forged or counterfeit currency notes have been detected.
mandatory_reports.submission_deadline: By the 15th day of the succeeding month.

kyc_officially_valid_documents_ovds: Proof of possession of Aadhaar number
Voter's Identity Card issued by Election Commission of India
Job card issued by NREGA duly signed by an officer of the State Government
Letter issued by the National Population Register containing name and address

pca_framework.title: Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) Framework
pca_framework.objective: Structured early-intervention mechanism by RBI to prevent bank insolvency and protect depositor money.

monitored_indicators.indicator: CRAR (Capital to Risk Weighted Assets Ratio) & Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) Ratio

mandatory_restrictions: Restriction on dividend distribution and remittance of profits
Restrictions on domestic or overseas expansion
Cap on lending to high-risk sectors

exam_traps.trap: Thinking SARFAESI Act can be used to auction agricultural farmland.
exam_traps.fact: Section 31(i) of SARFAESI Act explicitly EXCLUDES agricultural land from securitisation and enforcement.

exam_traps.trap: Believing a person with ₹5 Lakh in Savings and ₹5 Lakh in FD in the same bank is insured for ₹10 Lakh.
exam_traps.fact: DICGC insurance of ₹5 Lakh applies to the AGGREGATE of all deposit accounts of that person across all branches of the SAME bank in the same capacity.

exam_traps.trap: Thinking Low Risk KYC accounts need re-KYC every 5 years.
exam_traps.fact: Low Risk is every 10 years, Medium Risk is every 8 years, and High Risk is every 2 years.

exam_traps.trap: Assuming IBC corporate resolution time limit is 180 days with no maximum cap.
exam_traps.fact: CIRP is 180 days + 90 days extension, with a strict statutory maximum outer cap of 330 days including litigation.
